KEY MESSAGE 1...A powerful coastal storm will continue to bring 
severe impacts to the region into this evening due to damaging 
high winds accompanied by heavy rainfall. The storm departs 
overnight into Friday. 

Synoptics:

As of 700 PM, the initial center of low pressure was located 
over Delmarva and weakening, while a new center was forming
along the border of West Virginia and Virginia while the system
as a whole continues to move northward. The arrival of the
initial low center into the southeastern portion of our area has
begun to lessen the pressure gradient across that portion of the
area. However, for the remainder of the region, a very strong
gradient remains with high pressure continuing to linger across
the Canadian Maritimes. Storm impacts are discussed in further 
detail below:

Impacts:

Winds: The most severe impact from this storm aside from coastal 
flooding (see separate coastal flooding key message below) will be 
from damaging high winds. While the peak of the winds has likely
passed, impacts remain possible with strong winds of 50-60 MPH
continuing along with the ground becoming more saturated with
the rainfall. Widespread tree damage and power outages remain
possible. Otherwise, winds continue to diminish south to north 
through the evening period into the early overnight.

While the winds will subside for a time tonight, they will pick back 
up again for Friday with southwest winds potentially gusting 30 to 
40 mph. This may hamper clean up efforts. 

Rainfall/flooding threat: Given recent dryness and the progressive 
nature of this system, freshwater flooding does not appear to be as 
significant of a concern (compared to the high winds and tidal 
flooding). Rainfall is also beginning to taper off, though some
heavier pockets remain scattered across Delmarva and the New
Jersey coastal plain. However, with a widespread 1 to 3 inches
of rain already fallen and another 1-1.5 inches possible, some
localized flooding remains possible. The biggest threat will be
urban flooding as well as flooding of low lying and poor 
drainage areas. Some of the more sensitive creeks and streams 
could also exceed flood stage. Some showers are likely to 
linger on Friday, especially northwest of I- 95, but any 
rainfall on Friday will be inconsequential.

Timing: Heaviest rain and strongest winds through early this 
evening before the low starts pulling away. 

Friday will be windy (winds not nearly as strong as today) with some 
showers around. Even Saturday will be breezy (but less so than 
Friday) but otherwise the weather over the weekend will be more 
tranquil. 


KEY MESSAGE 2...Significant tidal flooding is expected to 
continue tonight, with lingering impacts into Friday. 

A high impact, powerful storm will continue moving up the 
eastern seaboard today. The strong onshore fetch from this storm
has resulted in significant tidal flooding, with major flooding
occurring today along the New Jersey and Delaware coast as well
as areas on the western side of Delaware Bay.

High tide is ongoing at this hour (about 8 PM) along the
Atlantic coastline. Winds have yet to die down along the
northern New Jersey coast, which is likely to result in major
tidal flooding at Sandy Hook and Perth Amboy. Winds have died
down over the past few hours further south, with only minor to
moderate tidal flooding expected. Further south over southern
Delaware, where winds have been more southerly for a while now,
only minor tidal flooding is expected. This should be the last
tide cycle on the Atlantic coastline to see flooding over
moderate, but trends will be monitored.

With flow turning more southerly, a surge of water is expected
to move up towards the upper Delaware Bay and tidal Delaware
River. Add in a freshwater component from runoff (about 1.5 to
2.5" of rain is expected across the I-95 corridor when all is
said and done). This will result in potential moderate flooding
with the next two high tide cycles at Reedy Point, Philadelphia,
and Burlington. Ended up upgrading the Coastal Flood Advisory to
a Coastal Flood Warning through early Saturday morning. 

A similar situation is expected along the Chesapeake Bay.
Southerly flow is pushing water up the bay, which will result in
tidal flooding. We saw high end minor tidal flooding/low end
moderate flooding with the most recent high tide. Tide levels
will slowly decrease but widespread minor tidal flooding is
expected with the next two high tide cycles through Saturday
morning. Coastal Flood Advisory remains in effect for the
Eastern Shore. 

Continue to follow any directions from local officials. Roads 
will become impassible near high tide in many coastal areas.
